 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 6, 2026, 20:02 IST CBSE releases class 10 and 12 datesheet for 2027 The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has released the official date sheet for the Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations 2027. According to the schedule, examinations for both classes will commence on February 16, 2027.
 Students can access the complete timetable on the board's official website, cbse.gov.in . The date sheet provides subject-wise examination dates, timings, subject names and subject codes. It also carries important instructions that candidates are expected to follow on examination days. The board has advised students to read the entire document carefully and to consult the official website regularly for any further notifications.

 CBSE 10th and 12th Class Practicals/Project Assessment 2027 begin 1-Jan-2027 
 Class 10 and 12 Practical/Internal Assessment ends To be notified 
 The announcement follows a pattern similar to that of the previous academic year. Last year, the board issued a tentative date sheet on September 24 and published the final schedule on October 30. The 2027 timetable has been released in early November, ahead of the examination period.
 As in previous years, the board examinations are expected to be conducted in pen-and-paper mode between February and March, at examination centres across India and abroad.
 Practical and internal assessments 
 Separately, the board has announced the schedule for practical examinations, project assessments and internal assessments for the 2026-27 academic session. For schools in winter-bound regions, these will be conducted from November 9 to December 19, 2026. 
 A detailed schedule for regular schools has also been made available by the board.
 Correction of candidate details 
 The board has also opened the List of Candidates (LOC) correction window for Classes 10 and 12 for the 2026-27 session. Schools may rectify students' details on the official portal until November 7. Students and parents are not permitted to make corrections directly; all changes must be submitted through the respective schools. Schools are therefore urged to verify records promptly, as inaccuracies in submitted data may create difficulties at later stages of the examination process.
 Preparation resources 
 To assist candidates in their preparation, CBSE has made sample question papers available on its academic portal. These papers familiarise students with the structure of the question papers, the pattern of questions and the marking scheme for different subjects. Students are encouraged to use these resources to practise under timed conditions and to identify areas requiring further revision.
 With the examination commencing in February, students now have a defined timeframe within which to plan their revision. Educators generally recommend that candidates prepare a structured study schedule aligned with the date sheet, allocate adequate time to subjects with longer gaps between papers, and complete practical and internal assessment requirements well in advance.
 Parents and schools are advised to rely exclusively on information published on the official CBSE website, and to avoid unverified messages circulating on social media, which may contain inaccurate or outdated information.
